messages.content: You are designing a reusable native parameter editor for an existing scientific predictor. Return one JSON object with keys design (object) and source (Python source string). Only the supplied model interface and observed-feedback contract are available. Do not request or infer held-out experiment outcomes. Do not use network, files, subprocesses, torch, autograd or optimization libraries. The Python source may use numpy as np (provided by the harness), numeric builtins, lists and dictionaries. No imports. It must define recipes() and class NativeMLPEditor with the exact interface specified below. Design the numerical mechanism yourself from the model computation; it must actually change native model parameters, not add a post-hoc scorer.

Research objective: improve ranking of unassayed genes by a previously trained functional predictor as assay feedback arrives. This construction test will use HepG2 growth, with the original fixed gene folds and three existing model-training seeds. You will receive no real assay outcomes, model tensors, prior effect sizes, query labels or results during construction.

Model computation: a trained molecular-feature encoder produces a final hidden preactivation z_g in R^d. Functional score is f(g) = max(z_g,0) @ w + b, with d=128 in this implementation. The last hidden affine bias is beta. A native edit may change the output weights w and/or beta. For theta=[w,beta], the exact edited score is max(z_g + (beta_new-beta),0) @ w_new + b. Earlier weights, scalar output bias b and RNA-output weights stay fixed. Your cache z contains observations only; the deployment harness later applies the returned vector to the original functional.weight and trunk.2.bias and verifies original forward/save/reload. Each invocation starts from the original checkpoint, not a previously compounded edit.

Interface: recipes() returns a deterministic nonempty list of at most 12 JSON-serializable dictionaries, each with unique string id and any numerical settings you need. NativeMLPEditor(preactivation,w,bias,hidden_bias,seed) stores copies and exposes .base = concatenate([w,hidden_bias]). Its predict(vector,rows=None) must implement the exact native score above. Its propose(rows,y,recipe) uses only feedback rows and their standardized observed outcomes y (matching rows), returns a finite float64 vector of length 2*d containing NEW parameter values, and is deterministic for a given input/seed. preactivation can contain held-feedback rows, but propose must inspect only preactivation[rows] and y. Do not inspect other rows even for fitting feature normalization. No use of query labels or identity-specific rules. Include a principled bounded/regularized estimate that respects the parameter-to-output relationship. Explain what is estimated, how evidence maps to native coordinates, and why those coordinates suit this model. You may choose output-only and a small joint hidden/output family; do not change architecture. Use ordinary numpy linear algebra; no iterative gradient fitting. Keep recipes small and inference efficient.

Researcher-specified validation (already implemented outside your program, do not implement or alter): fixed 3-fold splitting of acquired feedback; fit proposals on two folds and predict the third; retain only candidates whose mean held-feedback top-budget utility is at least the original; among those choose strictly lower mean held-feedback outcome-gap-weighted pairwise logistic ranking loss; include original/no-op; refit the selected recipe on all acquired feedback. This harness uses 75 feedback labels per role and evaluates original fixed Top20 and Top50 budgets on disjoint queries only after all predictions are sealed. Three within-block permuted proposal controls use the same recipe menu and validation. You are not responsible for the scientific data split or the acceptance metric, which are supplied by the researcher.

Output design fields: mutable_parameter_reason, discrepancy_to_update, regularization_and_budget, generated_vs_supplied (explicitly distinguish the fixed researcher validation from your proposal mechanism), and why_fixed_program_can_be_reused. Include concise explanation; do not claim guaranteed improvements. source must be runnable with only np plus standard numeric/list/dict builtins. Avoid module imports and file access. No Markdown fences.
